Hey OP! I've been playing WoW for 10 years. Truth be told, nothing will live up to the experience, but here are a few games that are similar:

*Old School Runescape (http://oldschool.runescape.com/): Runescape is a classic. Take the game in it's prime and have community driven updates; that's old school runescape. It lives up in open world, community, and you can have a lot of fun/meet a lot of buds. Some downsides are grinding, but if you listen to movies/tv shows etc. or talk to people it's much better. Quests are also a blast.

*Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn (http://na.finalfantasyxiv.com/pr/): Right now this is my favorite MMORPG. There are loading screens between zones, and you have to sub (13$ or 15$). But other than that, XIV is a perfect option from WoW. There is a trial if you'd like to try it. Honestly, everything about this game is amazing, and it gave me the thrill of joining a new world that only WoW has produced.

*Dungeons and Dragons Online: Free! This game has a lot of depth like WoW, perhaps too much. But you will get easily immersed in the world and have a blast; especially with some friends.

*Lord of the Rings Online: Great f2p game to get immersed in. The only problem for me is that I'm not too invested in the world of LotR.

*TERA: This game is an obvious rec, but I'm not much of a fan. It's a little too basic for me.

I keep picking up MMOs as they come out thinking this is going to be the one that has gameplay as good as WoW, but it never happens. WoW is literally the only true MMO (I play Elite: Dangerous (PC), and Destiny (Xbone), but I don't really consider them MMOs in the same sense as WoW) that held my interest for any length of time.

Doing an MMO right is hard, and nearly everyone seems to screw it up in fundamental ways.

Skyforge just released recently and is F2P. It's not as open as WoW is in that you have to port between zones but I've been having fun with it. It's free and the combat is really refreshing. Something I haven't had a chance to experience in an mmo recently. I say give it a try. Watch some videos on it. Read up about it.

One nice thing is that once you're through the tutorial the game lets you try all the classes before you decide which one to work towards. The leveling system reminds me of Path of Exile if you ever played that where you change class and play style by navigating a talent web.

If nothing else, it's free at least, so of it doesn't scratch your particular itch, you can just delete the game after.
